value.name: Rosa serves coffee from doorway
value.description: Rosa brings two cups of coffee to the parlor doorway, leaves them just inside without entering, and withdraws.
evidence: At one point Rosa appeared in the parlor doorway with two cups of coffee on a small tray. She did not come in. She set the tray down on the floor just inside the doorway, the way someone might set out food for a cat they did not want to startle, and withdrew.

value.name: Asha and Marcus exchange a look
value.description: Asha and Marcus silently acknowledge Rosa's behavior by looking at each other.
evidence: "She's going to have to stop doing that," Marcus said quietly.

value.name: Marcus says Rosa must stop
value.description: Marcus quietly remarks that Rosa will need to stop leaving coffee at the doorway.
evidence: "She's going to have to stop doing that," Marcus said quietly.

value.name: Asha postpones confronting Rosa
value.description: When Marcus asks if she will tell Rosa, Asha decides not to address it today.

value.name: Asha drinks the coffee
value.description: Asha and Marcus drink the coffee, and Asha notices its unusual sweetness and quality.
evidence: They drank the coffee. It was very good coffee, made in a way Asha did not know how to make coffee, with a faint sweetness in it that was not sugar.

value.name: Asha reflects on Rosa's long service
value.description: Asha thinks about Rosa's thirty-one years of learning the family's preferences and her current inheritance.
evidence: She thought about a woman who had stood in this kitchen for thirty-one years learning what each member of a family liked and not liked, and she thought about that woman now sitting in a dining room having been told she owned a third of the building

value.name: Asha signs the petition
value.description: At a little past one, Asha signs the petition.
evidence: At a little past one she signed the petition.

value.name: Marcus packs up the boxes
value.description: Marcus finishes the paperwork and gathers the boxes to leave.
evidence: They carried the boxes back out through the front hall.

value.name: Voices continue behind closed dining room door
value.description: As Asha leaves, she hears Lucia, Rosa, and Daniel talking quietly behind the closed dining room door.
evidence: The dining room door was closed now.
From behind it Asha could hear the low murmur of voices — Lucia's, mostly, and occasionally Rosa's, and once Daniel's, not arguing, just speaking.

value.name: Asha leaves without listening
value.description: Asha chooses not to stop and listen, and lets Marcus open the front door as they depart.
evidence: She did not stop to listen.
